findings.title: Alias resolution has no read path; any spec that resolves aliases changes pinned InstanceClaims privileges
evidence: src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/Migrations/20261119000000_PublisherIdentities.cs: REVOKE ALL ON alias_reservations FROM gozleme_app; GRANT INSERT only; RLS enabled with only alias_reservations_insert policy
src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/TableClassification.cs InstanceClaims[alias_reservations] = {INSERT}; RlsCatalog.InstanceViolationsAsync requires exact privilege set equality (RlsCatalogTests)
docs/specs/005-publisher-identities/contracts/namespace.md: 'Alias resolution (alias -> canonical ID) is not offered in v1 ... needs security review'
spec.md assumptions: resolving an alias or canonical ID across organizations belongs to discovery (GOZ-0012) and federation
findings.recommendation: Maintainer decides before the GOZ-0012 plan, after a security review. Option A: grant gozleme_app SELECT on alias_reservations with a policy limited to aliases whose capability the caller can see (needs GOZ-0012 visibility; still leaks reservation existence of private aliases unless the policy joins visibility). Option B: a narrow SECURITY DEFINER helper resolve_alias(alias) returning a canonical ID only when visible, added to DefinerHelpers and pinned. Option C: no alias resolution in MVP; inputs require canonical IDs and aliases stay display-only. Recommended: B or C. Each option changes RlsCatalogTests pins deliberately.
options: A: SELECT grant + visibility-joined policy on alias_reservations
B: pinned SECURITY DEFINER resolver returning only visible canonical IDs
C: no alias resolution in MVP; canonical IDs required as input

src/Gozleme.Api/Publishers/PublisherEndpoints.cs:391 alias rendered from publisher.Handle, so a suspended publisher keeps showing its old handle
findings.recommendation: Key references, pins, indexes and URLs by UUID/canonical ID; resolve handle -> publisher only through the held claim; federation key pins on publisher ID.

findings.title: Suspension by reclaim is permanent and cannot be lifted without a schema change
evidence: src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/Migrations/20261119000000_PublisherIdentities.cs: handle_claims_guard makes released and reclaimed terminal; ux_handle_claims_publisher unique on publisher_id for every status, so a reclaimed publisher can never hold a claim again

no downstream prompt covers moderation, appeals or suspension lifting
findings.recommendation: Maintainer decides before GOZ-0039 clarification whether MVP needs to lift a suspension. Option A: accept permanent suspension for MVP (the affected organization registers a new handle; capabilities keep canonical IDs). Option B: GOZ-0039 or a new spec adds an operator restore command, changing the guard and the publisher unique index. Option C: post-MVP moderation/appeals spec. Per-spec semantics of suspended publishers are routed to each spec's clarification (applied).
findings.decideBefore: GOZ-0039 clarification (semantics per spec: GOZ-0007 plan first)
options: B: operator restore in GOZ-0039 or a new spec
